draft.title: Volume and capacity of prisms
card: A prism has the same cross-section all along its length. Its volume is the area of the cross-section × the length.
Find the cross-section area first. For a triangle it is ½ × base × height, and for a rectangle it is length × width.
Capacity is how much a container holds. 1 cm³ holds 1 mL, and 1000 cm³ holds 1 L.
Example: a tank has a rectangular cross-section of 20 cm by 10 cm and is 50 cm long. Volume = 200 × 50 = 10 000 cm³, so its capacity is 10 000 mL, or 10 L.
draft.remember: Volume = cross-section area × length. Then 1000 cm³ is 1 L.

a.q: A prism has a triangular cross-section with a base of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. It is 10 cm long. What is its volume?
a.why: The triangle's area is ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm². The volume is 12 × 10 = 120 cm³. Using 6 × 4 = 24 cm² for the triangle gives 240 cm³, but that forgets the half.
a.clue: Find the area of the triangle first.

b.q: A fish tank is a rectangular prism 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres of water does it hold when full?
b.why: The volume is 50 × 30 × 40 = 60 000 cm³. Since 1000 cm³ holds 1 L, the tank holds 60 L. Giving 60 000 L mixes up cm³ with litres, because 60 000 is the number of mL.
b.clue: Find the volume in cm³, then divide by 1000.

problems.detail: The card gives a rectangle's area as 'length × width' right after using 'length' for the prism's length. A student could mix up the length of the cross-section with the length of the prism. 'Base × height' or 'width × height' would avoid the clash.

check.summary: The facts, the worked example and both questions are correct, and each question has one clear answer (120 cm³ and 60 L). The only issue is minor: the card uses 'length' both for the rectangle's side and for the prism, which could confuse some students.

final.title: Volume and capacity of prisms
card: A prism has the same cross-section all along its length. Its volume is the area of the cross-section \(\times\) the length.
Find the cross-section area first. For a triangle it is \(\frac{1}{2} \times\) base \(\times\) height, and for a rectangle it is width \(\times\) height.
Capacity is how much a container holds. \(1\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 mL, and \(1000\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 L.
Example: a tank has a rectangular cross-section of 20 cm by 10 cm and is 50 cm long. Volume \(= 200 \times 50 = 10{,}000\text{ cm}^{3}\), so its capacity is 10,000 mL, or 10 L.
final.remember: Volume \(=\) cross-section area \(\times\) length. Then \(1000\text{ cm}^{3}\) holds 1 L.

a.q: A prism has a triangular cross-section with a base of 6 cm and a height of 4 cm. It is 10 cm long. What is its volume?
a.why: The triangle's area is \(\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12\text{ cm}^{2}\). The volume is \(12 \times 10 = 120\text{ cm}^{3}\). Using \(6 \times 4 = 24\text{ cm}^{2}\) for the triangle gives \(240\text{ cm}^{3}\), but that forgets the half.
a.clue: Find the area of the triangle first.

b.q: A fish tank is a rectangular prism 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm high. How many litres of water does it hold when full?
